- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast spikes; adjust forecast upward by 10–30% for early spikes.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33) in recent days, model tends to over-forecast declines; adjust downward by 10–30% for early drops.
- Model consistently over-estimates short-term (1–3 day) volatility after sentiment shifts; apply smoothing filter or reduce amplitude of first 3 forecast points.
- Model under-estimates long-term (10+ day) trends when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; scale up forecast by 20–50% for horizon > 10 days.
- Overshoots after sharp sentiment reversals (e.g., from negative to positive) — cap forecast at 1.5x prior peak or 1.2x sentiment-adjusted baseline.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 2.5x historical mean for 3+ consecutive days, reduce by 20–40% unless sentiment confirms breakout.
- Sentiment-driven momentum: if sentiment > 0.67 for 5+ days, forecast should trend upward; if sentiment < -0.33 for 5+ days, forecast should trend downward — apply directional bias multiplier (1.15–1.35 for up, 0.85–0.75 for down).
